verses.1: God blessed Noah and his sons, saying to them, “Be fertile, multiply, and fill the earth.
verses.2: The fear of you and the dread of you will be upon every living beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the sky, upon everything that moves along the ground, and upon all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hand.
verses.3: Every creature that moves and lives shall be yours for food, as I gave you the green plants.
verses.4: But you must not eat flesh with its life—its blood—in it.
verses.5: For your own lives, your blood I will demand an accounting. From the hand of every beast I will demand it, and from the hand of humans, from the hand of each man’s brother, I will demand the life of a human.
verses.6: Whoever sheds the blood of a human, by a human shall their blood be shed, for in the image of God, God made the human.
verses.7: And you, be fertile, multiply, and fill the earth, and dominate it.
verses.8: Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:
verses.9: “I am establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
verses.10: and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the domestic animals, and every wild beast that is with you, all that came out of the ark, all creatures on the earth.
verses.11: I will establish my covenant with you, and never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
verses.12: God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:
verses.13: I have placed my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
verses.14: When I bring clouds over the earth, and the bow appears in the clouds,
verses.15: I will remember the covenant I made between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy every living creature.
verses.16: The bow shall be in the clouds, and I will see it to remember the eternal covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth.”
verses.17: God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and every living creature on the earth.”
verses.18: The sons of Noah who went out from the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
verses.19: These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was dispersed.
verses.20: Noah, a man of the soil, planted a vineyard.
verses.21: He drank of the wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent.
verses.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.
verses.23: But Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it on both their shoulders, and walked in reverse to cover their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
verses.24: When Noah awoke from his wine, he learned what his youngest son had done to him.
verses.25: He said, “Cursed be Canaan; a slave of slaves he shall be to his brothers.”
verses.26: He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to them.”
verses.27: “May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.”
verses.28: Noah lived for 350 years after the flood.
verses.29: The total length of Noah’s life was 950 years, and he died.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: The phrase "in its life" (בְּנַפְשׁוֹ) reflects the Hebrew's use of "nephesh" for "life" rather than "soul."
- v. 27: "Japheth" is a proper name, and the poetic structure of v. 27 is preserved, with the repetition of "Canaan be a slave to them."
- v. 28–29: The phrase "lived for" (וַֽיְחִי) is used to distinguish the time after the flood from the full length of his life.
raw:
[1] God blessed Noah and his sons, saying to them, “Be fertile, multiply, and fill the earth.

[2] The fear of you and the dread of you will be upon every living beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the sky, upon everything that moves along the ground, and upon all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hand.

[3] Every creature that moves and lives shall be yours for food, as I gave you the green plants.

[4] But you must not eat flesh with its life—its blood—in it.

[5] For your own lives, your blood I will demand an accounting. From the hand of every beast I will demand it, and from the hand of humans, from the hand of each man’s brother, I will demand the life of a human.

[6] Whoever sheds the blood of a human, by a human shall their blood be shed, for in the image of God, God made the human.

[7] And you, be fertile, multiply, and fill the earth, and dominate it.

[8] Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:

[9] “I am establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,

[10] and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the domestic animals, and every wild beast that is with you, all that came out of the ark, all creatures on the earth.

[11] I will establish my covenant with you, and never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”

[12] God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:

[13] I have placed my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

[14] When I bring clouds over the earth, and the bow appears in the clouds,

[15] I will remember the covenant I made between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy every living creature.

[16] The bow shall be in the clouds, and I will see it to remember the eternal covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth.”

[17] God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and every living creature on the earth.”

[18] The sons of Noah who went out from the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

[19] These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was dispersed.

[20] Noah, a man of the soil, planted a vineyard.

[21] He drank of the wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent.

[22] Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.

[23] But Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it on both their shoulders, and walked in reverse to cover their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.

[24] When Noah awoke from his wine, he learned what his youngest son had done to him.

[25] He said, “Cursed be Canaan; a slave of slaves he shall be to his brothers.”

[26] He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to them.”

[27] “May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.”

[28] Noah lived for 350 years after the flood.

[29] The total length of Noah’s life was 950 years, and he died.

---
Notes
- v. 4: The phrase "in its life" (בְּנַפְשׁוֹ) reflects the Hebrew's use of "nephesh" for "life" rather than "soul."
- v. 27: "Japheth" is a proper name, and the poetic structure of v. 27 is preserved, with the repetition of "Canaan be a slave to them."
- v. 28–29: The phrase "lived for" (וַֽיְחִי) is used to distinguish the time after the flood from the full length of his life.
